premise_checks.premise: A single optical method can deliver both the biomass signal and the metabolic signal in one measurement.
premise_checks.explanation: The sources show UV/Vis for biomass and Raman for metabolites as separate techniques used in the same reactor, and combination only as a hypothesis; no source shows one method covering both.

solution_options.performance_fit: Covers both targets in-line if fusion beats single methods
solution_options.cost_drivers: Two or more spectrometers, synchronised probes, fused-model development and validation
solution_options.fusion_note: Low-level fusion of UV-Vis ATR and Raman (and optionally fluorescence) spectra from the same sampling spot, synchronised to a common time step. Each method keeps its own calibration block with block scaling so no method dominates. The fused model must beat the best single method on independent runs, otherwise the extra instrument is dropped.

citations.quote: the data from each method must be obtained simultaneously.
If the variables have different units of measurement, the data should be normalized in some way, for example, using an autoscaling algorithm.

chemometrics_note: Each method needs its own calibration against the reference measurements (cell density, metabolite assays); validate on held-out runs and use scatter-appropriate preprocessing, since physical turbidity variation can mimic composition change.
realtime_tracking_note: The goal is continuous in-line tracking of growth and metabolic changes; acquisition rate and time resolution should be set so early changes are captured, and any fused data must be normalised to a common time step.
future_direction: If the feasibility study succeeds, a compact dedicated sensor configuration for the validated method(s) can be considered later for routine in-line use.

proposal.what_would_change_it: Defining the metabolite targets (Q1) and the actual OD range (Q3) could shift the technique choice, for example reopening a transflection geometry if the broth stays clear, or adding fluorescence if a fluorophore is accepted (Q5).
proposal.next_step: Run a multi-method lab feasibility trial on representative broth samples with independent reference measurements, single methods first.

brief_answer: Test two single methods first in a lab feasibility study: a UV-Vis ATR probe for the biomass-related turbidity signal, which tolerates the broth becoming optically dense, and a Raman probe for the metabolite fingerprint. Fluorescence is worth adding only if your team defines a fluorescent marker. Avoid NIR transmission, which fails as the broth thickens. Still open: which metabolites define the metabolic signal, the OD range, and your reference methods and go/no-go criteria.
